stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that \( x(t) = 2 \ln{\left(t^{2} + 1 \right)} \) and \( y'(t) = 5 e^{\frac{t}{4}} \sin{\left(t \right)} \) for \( t \ge 0 \). Using a calculator, find \( x''(1) \) and \( y''(1) \), the components of the acceleration of the particle at \( t = 1 \). Show the setup for the calculations, and give each value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The component given as a velocity is differentiated once, \( \frac{5 e^{\frac{t}{4}} \sin{\left(t \right)}}{4} + 5 e^{\frac{t}{4}} \cos{\left(t \right)} \) at \( t = 1 \) gives about 4.819.
The component given as a position is differentiated twice, \( - \frac{4 \left(t - 1\right) \left(t + 1\right)}{\left(t^{2} + 1\right)^{2}} \) at \( t = 1 \) gives about 0.000.
worked_solution.rule_named: second derivative of a position component

worked_solution.text: The acceleration at \( t = 1 \) is \( x''(1) \approx 0.000 \) and \( y''(1) \approx 4.819 \).

options.label: \( x''(1) \approx 2.000 \) and \( y''(1) \approx 4.819 \)
options.derivation: each given component differentiated once, so the position component yields its velocity, not its acceleration

options.label: \( x''(1) \approx 2.000 \) and \( y''(1) \approx 5.402 \)
options.derivation: the velocity vector at the time reported as the acceleration

options.label: \( x''(1) \approx 4.819 \) and \( y''(1) \approx 0.000 \)
options.derivation: the two components written in the wrong order
